chapter: Hampton and Basie: tours and road life
title: Basie's hiring through recommendations; his heart attack
summary: Players were usually recommended by sidemen, and Royal blames Basie's inactivity for his heart attack.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, when it came to hiring somebody new, did he ever have any (inaudible)?

He usually had somebody in his band go out and recommend them. I was probably recommended in some way by Clark Terry or something like that. Then, all of a sudden, he would remember, 'Yeah, I remember him. He was the guy that did such and such a thing. Yeah, he's good. He's good.' But take somebody else to remember and he'd go to somebody else and tell him, 'Who would be the one for this?' And they were usually hired by somebody else in the band. When they're fired, they usually end up somebody's done the dirty work somewhere along the way there to get them fired. That's the way those --
How did he have a heart attack? He shouldn't have any stress at all.

Can't understand it. I think his heart attack came from his inactivities. He wouldn't walk anywhere. He wouldn't run anywhere. He wouldn't exercise nothing. He did nothing as much as possible. He did nothing. And so, that's
how he had a heart attack probably. I'm no doctor. But inactivity sometimes causes things to happen. If you don't use it, you lose it.
